item.research_question: How does aluminum addition and temperature variation affect the generalized stacking fault energy (GSFE) and twinning ability of face-centered cubic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: First-principles calculations using the exact muffin-tin orbitals (EMTO) method with the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange-correlation functional and coherent-potential approximation (CPA); paramagnetic state modeled via disordered local magnetic moment approach; lattice constants derived from experimental data and thermal expansion coefficients.
item.test_conditions: Temperature range covering room temperature up to 600 K; Al concentrations of 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 at.%; paramagnetic state assumed.
key_findings: At room temperature for the Al-free alloy, intrinsic stacking fault energy (γisf) is -6 mJ/m² and extrinsic stacking fault energy (γesf) is 3 mJ/m².
Unstable stacking fault energy (γusf) and unstable twinning fault energy (γutf) are 285 mJ/m² and 281 mJ/m² respectively at room temperature.
Both γisf and γesf increase monotonously with increasing temperature and Al content.
Both γusf and γutf decrease monotonously with increasing temperature and Al content.
The hcp-fcc interfacial energy (σ) remains in the range of 4–7 mJ/m² and is weakly dependent on temperature and Al content.
Two twinning ability parameters (Ttw and rd) indicate that twinability decreases with increasing temperature or Al content.
The alloys remain prone to twinning even at 600 K and 8% Al content, as Ttw remains far above 1.
Negative γisf values are observed for the Al-free alloy below 400 K, consistent with the thermodynamic stability of the hcp phase at low temperatures.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the negative γisf at low temperatures to the thermodynamic stability of the hexagonal close packed (hcp) phase relative to the fcc phase. The increase in γisf with temperature and Al content is linked to the changing free energy difference between hcp and fcc lattices, while the decrease in unstable fault energies is observed as a monotonic trend. The interfacial energy is derived from the difference between the calculated γisf and the structural energy difference (γ0), showing weak dependence on composition and temperature.
item.limitations: The study notes that the current twinning parameter (rd) cannot explain the observation of deformation twins in Al-free CrMnFeCoNi HEA below 400 K where the parameter predicts only stacking fault and full slip. Additionally, the authors state that predicting whether twinning is realized at elevated temperatures depends crucially on alloy preparation, microstructure, and strain rate, which are not captured by the current intrinsic energy parameters.
item.future_work: The authors propose that further theory is needed to resolve the discrepancy between the twinning parameter predictions and experimental observations at low temperatures. They also suggest that describing the effects of alloy preparation, microstructure, and strain rate requires further advanced models built upon the disclosed intrinsic energy parameters.
quotes: Upon Al addition or temperature increase, the intrinsic and extrinsic stacking fault energies increase, whereas the unstable stacking fault and unstable twinning fault energies decrease monotonously.
The current twinning parameter cannot explain this phenomenon. Further theory is needed to resolve this question.
